conviction_note: The H1 print will almost certainly beat OBC's own H1 plan (Q1 operating profit was already 52.7% of it, and new bond interest is lifting ordinary profit), but the street already sits 4.9% above the company's full-year OP guide and the stock is up 34% since the Q1 print and level with the consensus target price. So the reaction depends on whether OBC raises the full-year guide. It held the OP guide at Q2 in FY25 and FY26, and its last three Q2 prints moved -0.2%, -2.9% and -0.7%. That gives a small negative lean (p_up 46) on a 4% scale. The findings sum to -0.7, which is close in sign and size to the scaled -0.32.
bar: Company H1 plan: sales 27,619 / OP 12,479 / ordinary 13,254 (JPY m), from the Q1 tanshin, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260722/140120260721596926.pdf. Market bar: IFIS FY27 consensus as of 2026-10-26 is sales 58,890 / OP 27,798 / ordinary 29,808, against company FY guidance of 57,500 / 26,500 / 28,260 (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=4733). The IFIS H1 consensus was 'roughly equal' to the plan in July (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/4733_20260722_act_20260722_153008_3). No current H1 consensus was found, so print_vs_bar is my estimated H1 operating profit (about 12,900-13,200, +3 to +6% on plan) against a street H1 that I assume has risen since Q1. That assumption is not sourced, so findings that depend on the H1 bar are capped small.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register as of 2026-10-26: 0.48% (one seller), down 0.02pt, so shorts are covering slightly, not building (baseline, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). 信用倍率 is 2.22 (kabutan page, 2026-10-27), so margin longs are not crowded. There is no option skew. The 20-day run-up is +14.81%, and the stock is up +34% from the 2026-07-23 close of 7,015 to the 9,398 spot. Baseline priced_lean_pct is -0.586, mostly the run-up. The IFIS consensus target price is 9,425, 0.08% above spot. Sell-side is uniformly bullish and was raising targets into the print: GS 9,800→10,300 (2026-09-10), Morgan Stanley 7,500→10,000 (2026-09-14), JPM 8,500→9,000 (2026-08-19).

findings.finding: H1 should beat the company's own H1 plan. Q1 operating profit of 6,577m is already 52.7% of the 12,479m H1 plan; last year Q1 was 51.3% of plan and H1 landed +2.9% above it. That points to H1 OP of about 12,900-13,200m. Ordinary profit should beat by more, because new interest income (219m in Q1 against 2k a year earlier, from the 54bn of securities bought in FY26) left Q1 non-operating income at 552m against 775m planned for the whole half. That suggests H1 ordinary of about 14,000-14,400m against the 13,254m plan, and kabutan/IFIS headline the 経常 line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY24 Q2 (2023-10-24): H1 OP 8,162 against an initial 6,920 (+18%); stock prev close→D+1 -0.2%. FY26 Q2 (2025-10-28): H1 OP 11,160 against 10,850 plan (+2.9%); -0.7%. On this name an H1 beat against plan has not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Anyone can compute this progress rate from the Q1 tanshin, and the IFIS FY ordinary consensus (29,808, +18.2%) already sits 5.5% above the company plan, which is what it would look like if the street had absorbed the Q1 run-rate and the interest income. What may be left is the size of the ordinary-profit beat on the headline, if the street H1 has not fully adjusted for the bond interest. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Q1 beat IFIS Q1 consensus by 12.8% (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/4733_20260722_act_20260722_153008_3), and the FY26 H1 comparison comes from https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251028/140120251027579217.pdf. Both read the same company figures, so they are not independent of the Q1 tanshin.

findings.finding: The forecast decision is the swing item. Street FY OP (27,798) is 4.9% above OBC's 26,500 guide, and OBC's own record at Q2 is conservative. In FY25 it held OP at Q2 and revised only net profit for a securities gain (2024-10-29 tanshin). In FY26 it held at Q2 and then finished below its own guide (23,580 against 24,000). Against that, the 奉行11 maintenance end (Dec 2026) and support end (Apr 2027) are a dated migration deadline, which Q1 named as a growth driver. The FY24 invoice-system deadline year is the one recent year OBC raised at Q2. Net: a hold, the larger single probability, would leave the stock short of a street that has priced a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY25 (OP guide held, NI raised): -2.9%. Q2 FY26 (held): -0.7%. Q3 FY26 (2026-01-26, dividend raised, OP guide held): -5.9%. Q2 FY24 (raised): -0.2%. Q3 FY25 (2025-01-24, dividend raised): +8.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus gap is public, but the decision is not. With the stock at the consensus target price after a 34% run, the price looks like it assumes at least a raise to consensus. If it had priced a hold, the stock would sit near analysts' pre-Q1 targets (7,500-9,000) rather than at 9,400.
findings.independence: OBC's revision history comes from different documents: the FY25 Q2 tanshin (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20241029/140120241028504229.pdf), the FY26 Q2 tanshin (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20251028/140120251027579217.pdf), the FY26 actual against guide (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260421/140120260420506480.pdf) and kabutan's revision table (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=4733). The opposing evidence on the migration deadline is the Q1 tanshin commentary plus https://aurant-technologies.com/blog/obc-bugyo11-to-cloud-migration-guide/ (third party).

findings.finding: On real TDnet release dates (the baseline's history uses estimated dates that are off by 1-3 days), OBC's last three Q2 prints moved -0.2%, -2.9% and -0.7% from the prior close to D+1. They fell whether the guide was raised or held. This print arrives after a +34% run since Q1, with the stock at the consensus target price.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly the free control: run_up_20d already carries the run. What it adds is the name-specific record of Q2 prints being sold at real release times. Shorts are covering, not building, and margin is not crowded, so no visible seller is positioned for this.
findings.independence: Release dates and times come from kabutan's disclosure list (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4733&nmode=3) and OBC's IR calendar (https://www.obc.co.jp/corporate/ir/calendar). The prices come from Yahoo.

findings.finding: A capital-return surprise is unlikely at this print. The 65-yen interim is already in the plan, the FY27 plan payout is 50.5% against a stated policy of 'about 45%', and OBC's last two dividend increases came at Q3 (2025-01-24, 2026-01-26), not Q2. OBC has never announced a buyback in this record.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY25 dividend raise: +8.4%. Q3 FY26 dividend raise: -5.9%. No Q2 dividend change in FY25 or FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price. This is filed to record that the second item of the bar hierarchy is expected to be empty. The upside tail is a dividend raise bundled with an FY raise.
findings.independence: The Q3 dividend-revision disclosures are listed at https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4733&nmode=3.

outside_window.finding: 奉行11 program maintenance ends at the end of December 2026 and support at the end of April 2027 (third-party summary). That makes FY27 H2 the peak of migration demand, with a possible pull-forward hangover in FY28. This bears on the FY28 guide in April 2027, not on this print.

release_time_source: kabutan 2026-10-26 schedule lists 4733 under '取引時間中の発表' (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=4733&b=n202610260989). Prior releases on kabutan's disclosure list: Q2 FY26 2025-10-28 15:00, Q3 2026-01-26 15:00, FY 2026-04-21 15:00, but Q1 FY27 2026-07-22 15:30. So 15:00 is the likely time, and 15:30 cannot be excluded.
bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: the central item. The street is 4.9% above the FY OP guide, and OBC held at Q2 in FY25 and FY26 but raised in the FY24 deadline year. Returns: none expected (dividend raises come at Q3, interim 65 already planned, no buybacks). New-year guide: not applicable at H1. Quarter: H1 OP is likely +3-6% on plan and ordinary +6-9%, against own Q1 progress history of 51.3% (FY26) vs 52.7% now; mostly priced by the consensus.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the run-up/priced lean (-0.59) and slightly extends it through the guidance-hold habit, so much of it may be in the price. The strongest positive the release could carry is an FY OP raise to or above the 27,798 consensus driven by the 奉行11 migration deadline, perhaps with a dividend raise. I looked for it and weighted it in finding 2's +2.5 upper bound and in p_up 46 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Open question 4 (a run-in sized as a negative went wrong once) and rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): cut the positioning/Q2-history finding from -0.5 to -0.3, and moved p_up from 44 to 46, so expected_move went from -0.48 to -0.32
Rule 1 (negatives resting on a public series): left finding 2 standing, because it rests on the forecast decision the release adds, not on a visible miss; finding 1 is already sized as mostly priced
